title: Contact Slowed and Reverb Maker
description: How to send a correction, a source, or a question about how Slowed and Reverb Maker checks public facts.
heroText: Slowed and Reverb Maker is one free browser tool, not a reference site about other people's products: it has no accounts, no billing and no support tiers. This page says how a message reaches the maker of the site, what to put in a report so it can be reproduced, and what the tool will not pretend to do. A message about a file that will not render or a sentence that does not match the tool is the most useful kind there is.

sections.title: How to reach us
sections.body: There is no ticket desk, no account queue and no billing here — the whole product is one page that runs in your browser. Once the site is live on its own domain, its footer carries the address that reaches the maker directly, and every message there is read by the person who builds and maintains the tool. Until then the site runs on a staging domain and nothing you send is being collected.

sections.title: How a correction lands
sections.body: A guide sentence that no longer matches the tool gets rewritten in the next build of that page, and the checked date under its headline moves with it. Corrections are made from something we can reproduce — the file you loaded and the settings you used — so a report that names both is fixed the same week. One report does not take a page down, and a claim we cannot reproduce is corrected rather than repeated.

sections.title: What this page cannot promise
sections.body: This site hosts one tool and writes about it. It cannot take payments or issue refunds because it sells nothing, cannot recover a file it never received, cannot clear or license a song for you, and cannot act for any artist, label or platform whose music you edit. The rights to the track you process stay yours to check before you publish the result. What this page can do is fix the tool and the sentences around it.

sections.title: What to include in a report
sections.body: Name four things: the page or the control that went wrong, the audio format and length you loaded, the exact settings on the console at the time — speed, pitch, reverb, bass, trim and preset — and what you expected instead. A browser name and a screenshot help. A report about a render is easiest to check on a short file: five seconds of a hook is enough to show a render that stops early or a file that comes out at the wrong length.

sections.title: If a tool result looks wrong
sections.body: Every step runs on your own device, so the method is on the page: the speed slider slows the playback and drags the pitch down with it — about four semitones at 0.80× — the pitch field adds whole semitones on top of that, reverb runs through a decaying room impulse, and bass through a low-shelf boost at 120 Hz. The render is sized from those same numbers, so a slow preset gives a longer file and a sped-up one a shorter file. If what you hear or download disagrees with that, send the preset and the export format and it can be reproduced here.

sections.title: When a change shows up
sections.body: A fix ships with the next build of the page, and the checked date under the headline moves with it. There is no account to escalate and no queue to join: a message about a refund, a licence or a takedown of someone else's song is answered by pointing at the rights holder rather than by an action here. Reports that arrive with a file, the settings and the format can be reproduced and fixed; ones without them usually cannot.
